newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Home adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Home adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: U.S. Home Corp said Friday it adopted a stockholder rights plan to assure shareholders fair value in the event of any proposed takeover of the company. U.S. Home said the plan was not adopted in response to any acquisition attempt and it is not aware of any such effort.

"The rights plan does not, nor is it intended to, prevent a takeover but rather is a measure to encourage anyone seeking to acquire the company to negotiate with the board," said U.S. Home's Chairman Robert Strudler.
The plan sets a on-taxable dividend distribution of one preferred stock purchase right, with an exercise price of $80, on each common and convertible preferred share, the company said.

The rights are redeemable by the board at $.01 per right until a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of the company's common stock, or an institutional stockholder acquires 20 percent or more of the common stock, U.S. Home said.
